definition: Trading date of the study.
kdb symbol, from the equity reference table.
ID_ISIN of the listing. The key the CAS whitelist and the index weights are matched on.
Company name, from config/nifty50_weights.csv. Empty for non-members.
NIFTY50 (index member), CAS_OTHER (CAS-eligible, not in the index) or NONCAS (the control arm).
True when the ISIN is in the CAS whitelist, i.e. the name closes via the auction.
True when the ISIN is a NIFTY 50 constituent per config/nifty50_weights.csv.
Published index weight. Empty for non-members and for a member whose weight the source did not publish.
ok = both the old-rule price and the auction print exist; no_old_rule_price; no_close_price; no_data.
Which VWAP fed effect_bps: last30-continuous (17:15-17:45, the default) or clock-1730-1800.
VWAP over [17:15; 17:45) HKT - the old rule (VWAP of the last 30 min of continuous) applied to today's session, which now ends at 17:45. The counterfactual close.
Sum of size over that window.
Number of records in that window.

VWAP over [17:30; 18:00) HKT - the clock window the old rule occupied pre-CAS. For a control name this is its actual official close; for a CAS name it contains the auction print itself and must not be used as the counterfactual.
Sum of size over that window.
Number of records in that window.

(px_old_rule_clock_1730_1800 / px_old_rule_last30_continuous - 1) * 10000. On a control name this is pure window artefact: what moving the 30-minute window 15 minutes later is worth on its own. The yardstick an index effect has to beat.
CAS reference price: size wavg price over [17:30; 17:45) HKT = 15:00-15:15 IST. Centre of the exchange's +/-3% band.
Sum of size over the reference window.
Number of records in the reference window.
Last price strictly before 17:45 HKT - the end of continuous trading.
Timestamp of that print, so a stale reference is visible.
Number of priced records up to 17:45 HKT.
First price inside [17:58; 18:00] HKT - the auction print. Order entry stops at a random instant in this window, so the print time is exogenous.
Timestamp of the auction print. Should cluster on one instant across names; a wide spread means the window is catching ordinary trades.
Volume that printed inside the close window - the auction size for this name.
Number of priced records in the close window.
Whole-day traded volume.
Volume from 17:45 HKT to the end of the day.
vol_after_continuous / vol_day * 100 - how much of the day migrated past the end of continuous.
vol_close_window / vol_day * 100 - how much of the day printed in the auction itself. The regressor for 'are the big contributors the names whose flow concentrated there'.
Previous session's close, from the equity reference table when it carries one. Feeds the whole-day reconciliation only.
(px_auction_close / px_prev_close - 1) * 10000 - the name's whole-day return, which the reconciliation aggregates into an index return.
px_auction_close - the old-rule price, in rupees.
effect_price / tick_size - the effect in exchange ticks. Under one tick is the price grid, not a move.
(px_auction_close / old-rule price - 1) * 10000 - what CAS changed for this name, against the close the old rule would have produced. The core measure.
(px_auction_close / px_last_continuous - 1) * 10000. Its gap to effect_bps is stale-last-print bias.
(px_auction_close / px_cas_reference - 1) * 10000 - directly comparable to the +/-300 bps band.
nifty50_weight_pct * effect_bps / covered weight. Sums exactly to the index effect, so a name's number is its share of the answer.
|contribution_bps| as a percent of the gross contribution across all names.
Trading date.
NIFTY50, CAS_ALL, NONCAS or NONCAS_MATCHED (the control restricted to the CAS group's p10-p90 of day volume).
Names in the group.
Names with status = ok, i.e. the ones every statistic below is computed on.
Sum of index weight behind the weighted number. Everything is renormalised over it.
The index effect: sum(weight * effect_bps) / sum(weight). The headline answer for NIFTY50.
Equal-weighted mean effect across names - what the average name did, as opposed to what the index did.
Median effect, robust to a single outlier name.
Dispersion of the effect across names.
Mean absolute effect - how much the mechanism moves prices regardless of direction.
Mean absolute effect in ticks, comparable across price levels.
Share of names whose effect is at least one tick - i.e. moved at all rather than sat on the grid.
Mean share of the day's volume that traded after continuous ended.
Mean window_shift_bps. On the control groups this is the artefact yardstick.
Names with a positive effect.
Names with a negative effect.
Names whose effect is exactly zero.
The matched control group's mean effect - market drift over the same clock window with no auction involved.
The group's effect minus control_drift_bps. The auction-specific part.
Official NIFTY 50 close supplied via --index-level, used to convert bps into points.
effect_bps_index_weighted / 10000 * index_level - the index effect in points.
Cross-sectional standard error of the effect across the group's names. An effect smaller than about twice this is not distinguishable from zero on this day.
